title: TrueNorth quest
description: One quest, `content/quests/<id>.json`. A quest is an ordered list of steps an ENGAGEABLE gives the player - a character, or a landmark the level places - and finishing the last step completes it. `giver` said `characterId` until ADR-0029, which encoded "a quest is offered by somebody" as a type and cost `peggys-cove` and `the-north` their quests, because both levels forbid drawing a figure of any kind at any scale and a plaque is not a figure. Question scheduling belongs to the domain - a step names the pool, it does not pick from it.

levelId.description: The level this quest is played on. The level document lists the quest id too. THIS SENTENCE USED TO SAY validate-content CROSS-CHECKS THE TWO AND IT DID NOT - `grep quest scripts/validate-content.mjs` finds a comment and no code, so the schema asserted a gate nobody had written, which is worse than an admitted gap because the claim stops the next person looking (ADR-0024, ADR-0029). Both directions are now checked by tests/unit/contracts/a-quest-giver-is-placed-on-its-level.test.ts.

giver.description: What offers the quest: a character the level places, or a point of interest on it - a plaque, an interpretive panel, a marker. UNBRANDED for the reason `questStep.targetId` is unbranded, and it is the same reason: what it names depends on how the level placed it, and a union of brands is not a shape a schema can state. WHICH KIND IT IS IS NOT DECLARED HERE, because the level already declares it by listing `characters[]` and `pois[]` apart; a second declaration on this document could disagree with the first. Required, and required for a reason ADR-0024 owns: a quest with no offerer folds to nothing to offer, nothing to decline and nothing to remind, and `app/ui/dialogue.ts` takes the giver name as a required option so an unnamed dialog cannot be built. Resolution is cross-document and is held by tests/unit/contracts/a-quest-giver-is-placed-on-its-level.test.ts: EXACTLY ONE placement on this quest's level has this id, and that placement declares `questId` equal to this quest. Zero is dangling and two is ambiguous, and the two fail differently. ADR-0029.

summary.description: One or two plain-language sentences shown in the quest log and announced in the live region when the quest is accepted.

declinedLine.description: What the giver says when the player chooses "Not now". Optional, and silence is a legal answer to a decline: a quest with no line for a moment says nothing rather than borrowing another quest's words (TN-DIALOGUE-02).

reminderLine.description: What the giver says when the player engages them while this quest is accepted and unfinished. ONE LINE FOR THE WHOLE QUEST, not one per step: the step's own `prompt` already says what to do now, and a per-step reminder is a second place for one instruction to be written differently. A quest that ever needs a per-step line gets an optional override on `questStep`, which is an additive change - removing a per-step field once four documents carry it is not (OQ-DIALOGUE-2).

afterLine.description: What the giver says when the player engages them after this quest is complete. Not `summary` read back: a summary is written in the present tense as an instruction, so reading it to somebody who has already done it is a screen describing a state the game is not in.

doneLine.description: What the completion card says this quest was, in the past tense. It is the quest's own words, not the global `quest.done.body` copy row that string was: "You skated to Parliament Hill and answered three questions" names a landmark, a locomotion mode and a count, and all three belong to one quest (ADR-0010).

questStep.title: Quest step document
questStep.description: One objective. `targetId` is deliberately an unbranded id: what it names depends on `kind` (a character OR A POINT OF INTEREST for talk, a POI for visit or collect, a question pool for answer), and a union of brands is not a shape a schema can state. `talk` gained the POI case with ADR-0029: on a level that may draw no figure, the thing the player taps to be told something is a plaque, and this field was already the right shape for that - `giver` was not, and that is what ADR-0029 fixed.

prompt.description: What the player is being asked to do, in plain language, roughly CLB 4.

subject.description: Which bank an `answer` step draws from. Required on `answer` steps and forbidden elsewhere.

count.description: How many questions an `answer` step asks. The quest says how many; the FSRS scheduler says which, from the player's own review state. A quest that named the ids would make the scheduler decorative, and a scheduler that ignored the quest would make the step unbounded - so the quest owns the count and the pool, and the domain owns the choice.

questionPool.description: Optional narrowing of the draw to these ids, still ordered and filtered by the scheduler. Absent means the whole subject bank is eligible, which is the normal case; present is for a step that must stay on one topic.

dialogue.description: Lines spoken when the step starts, and the whole of the quest's voice. REQUIRED on a `talk` step: it is what the giver says when the offer opens, and `app/bootstrap/quests.ts` refuses a `talk` step without it, because a giver who opens a dialog and says nothing is worse than a giver who is not offered. OPTIONAL on `visit` and `collect`, where it is what the player is told on ARRIVING at the target - drawn after that landmark's own card and before the question, under the speaker's name, so the place and whoever is commenting on it are never one voice. Absent there means that step is silent, and silence is the document's choice rather than a field nobody read (ADR-0024). NOT READ on an `answer` step: `readStep` does not look, so lines written there would validate and never be spoken. Subtitles are on by default, so this is the subtitle text as well as the dialogue text.

allOf.$comment: The draw specification belongs to `answer` steps and to nothing else, so a `talk` step cannot carry a stray subject or count that nothing reads. Only property names this object already declares appear here (ADR-0007).

then.$comment: `subject` and `count` are restated here as empty schemas ONLY to satisfy ajv's strictRequired lint, which asks that a property named in `required` be declared in the same subschema. They impose nothing: the real types are on questStep's own `properties` above and still apply, because a conditional subschema is evaluated against the same instance. Without this the file does not compile at all, which is how it shipped -- nothing exercised it until the first quest document existed.

speaker.description: Whose words these are: the engageable the player is reading or listening to, named as the level placed it - a character, or a point of interest. REQUIRED, and it is not the field to make optional if a panel feels speakerless: a screen reader is handed the dialog's accessible name before a word of prose, so a line with no source is a line the live region cannot attribute, and a landmark has a name already (`pois[].name`, bilingual, required). Unbranded and unresolved here for the same reason as `giver`; the cross-document gate resolves both on one pass. ADR-0029.

fact.description: Whether this line states a fact about Canada and, if so, its source and verification. "Welcome to Parliament Hill" is flavour; "Ottawa is Canada's capital" is a claim, and a wrong claim in an NPC's mouth is exactly as wrong as one on a question card (ADR-0003).

expression.description: Named face pose on the speaker's rig, resolved by the same name in Rive and in the sprite atlas. Absent leaves the rig's default. FORBIDDEN WHEN THE SPEAKER IS A POINT OF INTEREST: a plaque has no face and no mood, and `expression: "happy"` on one is a small lie that would reach `ICharacterRenderer` as a request for a rig that does not exist. That rule is NOT here and cannot be: this document does not know what its speaker is, and asking it to say would be the second declaration `giver` refuses. Per ADR-0024 the floor goes where the meaning is known, which is the level's placement, so the gate at tests/unit/contracts/a-quest-giver-is-placed-on-its-level.test.ts holds it. ADR-0029.
